blocks.content: DNH&DD's polity chapter centres on one structural fact common to several smaller UTs: it has no Legislative Assembly of its own and is directly administered by the Union Government through an Administrator. The chapter also tests the UT's unusual TWO-Lok-Sabha-seat status, unlike most single-seat UTs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, empowering Governors to adapt state laws.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) extends self-governance to tribal areas by empowering the Gram Sabha.
Tribal Advisory Councils (TAC) consisting of up to 20 members are established in Fifth Schedule states to advise on tribal welfare.
Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) under the Sixth Schedule enjoy extensive legislative, executive, and judicial powers in specific Northeastern states.
Articles 330, 332, and 335 provide constitutional guarantees for representation and affirmative action for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

blocks.content: DNH&DD is a Union Territory administered by the President of India through an Administrator, appointed under Article 239 of the Constitution — it has no elected Legislative Assembly, placing it in the same structural category as Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Ladakh (as opposed to Delhi, Puducherry and J&K, which do have assemblies).

As of 2026, the Administrator is Shri Praful Khoda Patel, in office since the UT's formation on 26 January 2020, making him the territory's first and, so far, only Administrator; he simultaneously holds the additional charge of Administrator of Lakshadweep since December 2020 — an unusual dual-UT administrative arrangement.

Day-to-day administration is run by an Advisor to the Administrator and a Secretariat structure, with separate directorates for Dadra & Nagar Haveli and for Daman & Diu still partially retained for continuity, even after the 2020 merger.
The Gram Sabha shall be competent to safeguard and preserve the traditions and customs of the people, their cultural identity, community resources, and the customary mode of dispute resolution.

The judiciary of DNH&DD falls under the jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court, reflecting the territory's historical and geographical proximity to Maharashtra/Gujarat rather than a dedicated High Court of its own.

cells: Administrator, appointed by the President of India under Article 239
Shri Praful Khoda Patel — in office since 26 January 2020 (first Administrator of the merged UT); also Administrator of Lakshadweep (additional charge, since Dec 2020)
None — directly administered, like Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Ladakh
2 — Dadra & Nagar Haveli (ST-reserved) and Daman & Diu (unreserved)
Panchayats (Dadra & Nagar Haveli, rural areas) + Municipal Councils (Silvassa, Daman, Diu)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: DNH&DD is one of the few UTs to send TWO members to the Lok Sabha despite having no Legislative Assembly — most no-assembly UTs (Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Ladakh) send only one. This is because the two erstwhile UTs retained their separate parliamentary seats even after administrative merger.

rows: Scheduled Areas in 10 states outside North-East India
Tribal Areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram
Advisory role to Governor regarding state laws
Direct law-making power on land, forests, and customary laws

items: Dadra & Nagar Haveli district — headquartered at Silvassa; the largest district by area and population, with a substantial Scheduled Tribe population.
Daman district — headquartered at Daman (also the UT capital); includes Moti Daman and Nani Daman, the historic twin settlements straddling the Daman Ganga estuary.
Diu district — headquartered at Diu town, on Diu island; the smallest district by both area and population.

cells: Urban local body for Silvassa town, Dadra & Nagar Haveli
Gram Panchayats operate in the rural, largely tribal areas of Dadra & Nagar Haveli under the Dadra and Nagar Haveli Panchayats Regulation

items: PESA Act 1996 explicitly mandates Gram Sabha approval for land acquisition, minor forest produce ownership, and control over local institutions in Scheduled Areas.
Difference between 5th and 6th Schedules: 6th Schedule applies exclusively to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram with Autonomous District Councils (ADCs).
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is a constitutional body established under Article 338A via the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

The Dadra & Nagar Haveli Lok Sabha seat is reserved for Scheduled Tribes, reflecting the district's majority-tribal demographic profile (Dhodia, Kokna/Kokni, Varli and other communities — detailed in Chapter 6).

Special land-transfer and tenancy protections restrict the sale/transfer of tribal agricultural land in Dadra & Nagar Haveli to non-tribals, similar in spirit to protective tribal-land regulations found in other Fifth/Sixth Schedule-adjacent tribal areas of India, aimed at preventing land alienation of the indigenous population.
DNH&DD = UT with NO Legislative Assembly; administered by an Administrator appointed by the President under Article 239.
Current (2026) Administrator: Praful Khoda Patel, since 26 Jan 2020 — also holds additional charge as Administrator of Lakshadweep.
2 Lok Sabha seats (Dadra & Nagar Haveli — ST-reserved; Daman & Diu — unreserved); 0 Rajya Sabha seats.
Judicially under the Bombay High Court.
3 districts: Dadra & Nagar Haveli (HQ Silvassa), Daman (HQ Daman), Diu (HQ Diu).
